uncited: Cubic Upsampling via Tiling is a deterministic, non-learning-based method for increasing the resolution of volumetric data by replicating existing voxels into larger blocks.

It solves the problem of generating a higher-resolution grid from a lower-resolution source without introducing interpolation artifacts or blurring, effectively performing nearest-neighbor expansion in 3D space.
Unlike bilinear or tri-linear interpolation which smooths boundaries, this method preserves sharp discontinuities in the data by strictly copying values.

It differs from neural super-resolution methods [3D Super-Resolution (SR) Module](6577-3d-super-resolution-sr-module.md) by requiring no training data or inference time, and from [3D Fast Bilateral Solver](6478-3d-fast-bilateral-solver.md) by ignoring edge-awareness constraints in favor of computational simplicity.
- `N_prev`: The resolution of the input volume along each axis (assumed cubic, i.e., $N_{prev} \times N_{prev} \times N_{prev}$).
- The input is conceptually treated as a 3D cube of shape $(N_{prev}, N_{prev}, N_{prev})$.
- The output is a 3D cube of shape $(N_{new}, N_{new}, N_{new})$.
- Memory layout is row-major (C-style) for both input and output 1D arrays.
Calculate the integer scale factor $s = N_{new} / N_{prev}$.
Reshape the 1D `input_values` array into a 3D array `cube` of shape $(N_{prev}, N_{prev}, N_{prev})$.
Tile `cube` along the Z-axis (dimension 2) by factor $s$.
This creates an intermediate array of shape $(N_{prev}, N_{prev}, N_{prev} \times s)$.
Tile the result along the Y-axis (dimension 1) by factor $s$.
This creates an intermediate array of shape $(N_{prev}, N_{prev} \times s, N_{prev} \times s)$.
Tile the result along the X-axis (dimension 0) by factor $s$.
This creates the final 3D array of shape $(N_{prev} \times s, N_{prev} \times s, N_{prev} \times s)$.
Reshape the final 3D array back into a 1D `output_values` array.
In a strict implementation, `tile_along_axis` would involve nested loops copying memory blocks.*
- **Non-integer Scale:** If $N_{new}$ is not divisible by $N_{prev}$, the method fails.
- **Memory Usage:** The output size grows by $s^3$.
For large $s$, this can exceed available RAM.
- **Data Type:** The method preserves the data type of the input.
No normalization or clamping is performed.
A specialized variant for upsampling ambient occlusion (AO) data in real-time rendering.
It extracts `BentNormal` and `SpecularOcclusion` components from a lower-resolution AO texture (`AoResolution`) to a higher-resolution target (`Resolution`).
- **Time Complexity:** $O(N_{new}^3)$, as every output voxel must be written.
The tiling operation is memory-bandwidth bound.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(N_{new}^3)$ for the output array.
Intermediate tiled arrays may temporarily double or triple memory usage depending on implementation.
- **Performance:** Extremely fast compared to interpolation or neural methods, as it involves only memory copying and reshaping.
- **Limitations:** Introduces "blocky" artifacts (aliasing) if the scale factor is large; does not recover high-frequency details lost in the original low-res volume; requires integer scale factors.
- **When to use:** Pre-processing for visualization, generating initial guesses for iterative solvers, or when sharp boundaries are critical and interpolation is undesirable.
- **When not to use:** When smooth transitions are required, or when the scale factor is non-integer.
This method is a fundamental technique in computer graphics for resizing volumetric data without learning-based approaches.
It is often used as a baseline or preprocessing step in volume rendering pipelines.
